headline: Approved federal pandemic funds for Villano and Keefe Center park work, youth summer program funding, and energy assistance agreements.
summary: Eleven residents spoke during public input. The administration reported on storm response, ICE activity, and a proposed Amazon drone delivery program. Council accepted a list of items sent to it, including the continued employment of the police and fire chiefs.
decisions: Approved modification of the conservation easement deed at 200 Leeder Hill Drive, unanimously.
Approved amending allocations of federal ARPA funds for maintenance at Villano Park and the Keefe Center park, unanimously.
Approved youth summer program agreements and spending from CYEP, DADS, and DCF funds, 12 in favor and 1 abstention.
Approved the September 14 meeting minutes, unanimously.
Accepted the list of items sent to Council for the submission calendar, 11 in favor, 1 opposed, and 1 abstention.
Approved energy assistance agreements for the Keefe and Miller centers, a Generation Power CT agreement, and a Brian Dolan agreement, unanimously.

plain_text:
TOWN OF HAMDEN, 
CONNECTICUT 
 
LEGISLATIVE COUNCIL 
 
SEPTEMBER 28, 2026 
 
MINUTES DRAFT 
 
Absent - Katie Kiely, President 
Present -Sean Cardwell, Pro Tem 
Present - Sarah Gallagher, Maj Leader 
Present - Bob Anthony, Min Leader 
Present - Tasha Hunt, Majority Whip 
Present - Tom Figlar, Minority Whip 
Present - Maurine Crouch 
Present - Doug Foley 
Present - Jeron Alston 
Present - Abdul Osmanu 
Absent - Rhonda Caldwell 
Present - Grace Teodosio 
Present - Adrian Webber 
Present - Ted Stevens 
Present - Tameeka Parks  
1. CALL OF THE MEETING AND TAKING OF THE ROLL 
The Legislative Council Regular Meeting, September 28, 2026.  The meeting was called 
to order by Pro Tem Cardwell at 7:09pm with those noted above in attendance.  President 
Kiely and Council member Caldwell were absent.  
  
 
Leadership Update –  
• Pro Tem Cardwell had no specific updates but noted that updates would be 
shared by the individual committees. 
  
 
News and Announcements –  
• An announcement was made regarding the Hamden Food Collaborative's 
September 30 community event, inviting residents to learn about food 
insecurity in Hamden and opportunities to support local hunger relief efforts. 
  
 
Celebrations –  
• There were no celebrations announced at this evening’s meeting. 
 
  
2. REPORT OF DEPARTMENTS, BOARDS, COMMISSIONS, AND COUNCIL LIAISONS  
  1. Upcoming Boards & Commission Meetings –  
Pro Tem Cardwell noted that Board/Commissions would be reviewed in Committees 
  2. Update from Department Heads – 
• Chief of Staff Peterson gave an update from Major Sendroff.  She started by 
thanking the Fire, Police, Public Works, and Parks Departments for their 
coordinated response to the recent storm. She also advised that, considering 
recent reports of increased ICE activity, the Administration is reaffirming its 
commitment to Trust Act and de-escalation training for public-facing 
employees, she further advised that the Administration is monitoring 
community concerns regarding Amazon's proposed drone delivery program 
and announced that Congresswoman Rosa DeLauro has included funding 
requests for capital improvements to the Miller Memorial Library and Senior 
Center, Brundage Library, and Keefe Community Center in the federal 
appropriations process.   
  3. Council Liaison Updates 
The upcoming School Building Committee Meeting was announced, and the public 
was invited to visit the Board of Education website to see their latest meeting 
minutes.
3. PUBLIC INPUT SESSION AND CORRESPONDENCE 
Eleven individuals came forward to give public comment.  The Public Input session was 
closed at 7:52pm.  
  
4. 
  
CONSENT CALENDAR 
Pro Tem Cardwell called for a motion to open the Consent Calendar: 
Motion: Gallagher 
Second: Parks  
 
Pro Tem asked if anyone wanted to remove any items from the Consent Calendar for 
additional discussion.  Items 1, 3, 4 and 5 were removed.  Item 6 was also removed as it 
had passed out of Council during the September 14th meeting. 
 
Pro Tem Cardwell called for a motion to pass item 2.   
 
 2. ORDER APPROVING MODIFICATION OF DEED OF CONSERVATION EASEMENT                       
200 LEEDER HILL DRIVE 
 
Motion: Foley 
Second: Osmanu.   
Vote: All in favor, 0 opposed, 0 abstentions.  The item passed unanimously. 
 
******************************  
 Pro Tem then called for a motion to open item 1. 
  1. ORDER FURTHER AMENDING AND RESTATING ALLOCATIONS OF 
CORONAVIRUS LOCAL FISCAL RECOVERY FUNDS (ALSO KNOWN AS 
AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN ACT FUNDS) (July 2026)  
 
Motion: Figlar 
Second: Teodosio  
 
Chief of Staff Peterson explained the funds were to be used for maintenance at 
Villano Park as well as the park at the Keefe Center.  She noted that they have the 
quotes and are ready to begin the work, stating that all work must be complete by 
December 31, 2026. After Ms. Peterson’s remarks, Council member Teodosio 
wanted to formally request an ARPA update. 
 
Vote: All in favor, 0 opposed, 0 abstentions.  Item 1 passed unanimously. 
 
****************************** 
  
Council member Crouch requested items 3, 4, and 5 be bundled.   
Motion Crouch 
Second: Gallagher  
Vote: 12 in favor, 0 opposed, 1 abstention (Hunt).  Motion to bundle passed 
unanimously.
3. ORDER APPROVING A MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT AND AUTHORIZING 
THE ACCEPTANCE AND EXPENDITURE OF FUNDS JULY 1, 2026- JUNE 30, 
2027, CT YOUTH EMPLOYMENT PROGRAM (CYEP) YOUTH SERVICES 
SUMMER PROGRAM  
  
  4. ORDER APPROVING A MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT AND AUTHORIZING 
THE ACCEPTANCE AND EXPENDITURE OF FUNDS JULY 1, 2026- JUNE 30, 
2027, DADS YOUTH SUMMER PROGRAM (DADS) 
  
  5. ORDER APPROVING A MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT AND AUTHORIZING 
THE ACCEPTANCE AND EXPENDITURE OF FUNDS JULY 1, 2026- JUNE 30, 
2027, DCF YOUTH SUMMER PROGRAM  
 
Pro Tem Cardwell called the vote to pass items 3, 4, 5. –  
Vote: 12 in favor, 0 opposed, 1 abstention (Hunt).  Items 3, 4, and 5 passed 
unanimously. 
 
****************************** 
  6. ORDER AUTHORIZING THE TOWN OF HAMDEN TO APPLY AND IF AWARDED 
ACCEPT AND EXPEND FUNDS FROM THE 2025 EDWARD BYRNE MEMORIAL 
JUSTICE ASSISTANCE GRANT FROM THE U.S. DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE -  
This item was pulled from the agenda because it passed out of Council on 
Monday, September 14th.  
  
5. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES 
A motion to approve the minutes from September 14th was made by Council member 
Parks and seconded by Pro Tem Cardwell.   
Vote: All in favor, 0 opposed, 0 abstentions.  Passed unanimously  
      
6. INFORMATION ITEMS  
 1. INFORMATION ITEM: EXPLORING THE FEASIBILITY OF HOSTING A HAUNTED 
HALLOWEEN EXPERIENCE IN THE MEMORIAL TOWN HALL 
Pro Tem Cardwell mentioned that a Haunted Halloween Hallway to be held at the 
Memorial Town Hall was being discussed.   
      
7. REGULAR AGENDA DELIBERATION AND ACTION  
* (Requires a vote of 2/3rds of the members present and voting for suspension of the rules 
under §14(a) of the Standing Rules) 
  
 
ACCEPTANCE OF ITEMS SENT TO COUNCIL FOR THE SUBMISSION 
CALENDAR: 
• ORDER APPROVING THE CONTINUED EMPLOYMENT OF EDWARD 
PAGE REYNOLDS CHIEF OF POLICE (Public Safety Committee) 
• ORDER APPROVING THE CONTINUED EMPLOYMENT OF SHELLY 
CARTER FIRE CHIEF (Public Safety Committee)
• ORDER PROVIDING FOR THE APPOINTMENT OF A MAYORAL 
APPOINTMENT JERMAINE B. ATKINSON - ASSISTANT FIRE CHIEF (Public 
Safety Committee) 
• ORDER AUTHORIZING THE TOWN OF HAMDEN TO ACCEPT AND 
EXPEND FUNDS FROM THE STATE OF CONNECTICUT, DEPARTMENT 
OF ECONOMIC AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT OFFICE OF 
BROWNFIELD REMEDIATION AND DEVELOPMENT PUTNAM TERRACE 
344-350 PUTNAM AVENUE (Engineering, Development & Municipal Planning Committee) 
• HAMDEN PUBLIC SCHOOLS SPECIAL EDUCATION SYSTEM REVIEW 
FUNDING REQUEST ($70,000) 
• INTERDEPARTMENTAL TRANSFER 25-26 FISCAL YEAR BUDGET 
PUBLIC WORKS ($11,787) 
• ACCEPTANCE OF TWO QUINNIPIAC UNIVERSITY VEHICLE GIFT 
DONATIONS OR HAMDEN POLICE DEPARTMENT 
• RESOLUTIONS OF ADMINISTRATION & SETTLEMENT COMMITTEE (4) 
• FINANCE TRANSFER FOR CLA 
• HAMDEN POLICE DEPARTMENT CATALIS CONTRACT (HPD WEBSITE - 
4-YEAR CONTRACT) 
• TRAFFIC SIGNAL AGREEMENT (AKRF) FOR CONSULTING 
ENGINEERING SERVICES - HAMDEN CENTER TRAFFIC SIGNAL 
IMPROVEMENTS 
Motion to accept: Gallagher 
Second: Parks 
Vote: 11 in favor, 1 opposed (Anthony) and 1 abstention (Teodosio). 
 
RECESS FOR COMMITTEE MEETINGS 
 
Pro Tem called for a motion to recess the Legislative Council meeting in order to hold 
the standing committee meetings. 
Motion: Gallagher 
Second: Osmanu  
 
RECOVENE LEGISLATIVE COUNCIL MEETING 
 
Pro Tem Cardwell reconvened the Legislative Council meeting at 10:14pm with the 
following members in attendance: Cardwell, Crouch, Figlar, Foley, Gallagher, Hunt, 
Osmanu, Parks, Stevens, Teodosio, and Webber. 
 
Resumption of the Regular Meeting Agenda: 
Pro Tem Cardwell called for a motion to suspend the rules.   
Motion: Parks 
Second: Crouch 
Pro Tem took a roll call vote: Caldwell Yes, Crouch Yes, Figlar Yes, Foley Yes, 
Gallagher Yes, Hunt Yes, Osmanu Yes, Parks Yes, Stevens Yes; Teodosio Yes; 
Webber Yes. 
Vote: 11 in favor, 0 opposed, 0 abstentions.
Pro Tem Cardwell then called for a motion to add these four items to the agenda:  
    1. ORDER APPROVING AGREEMENT WITH COMMUNITY ACTION AGENCY 
OF NEW HAVEN FOR CONNECTICUT ENERGY ASSISTANCE PROGRAM 
(CEAP) PROGRAM YEAR 2026-2027 KEEFE COMMUNITY CENTER 
  
    2. ORDER APPROVING AGREEMENT WITH COMMUNITY ACTION AGENCY 
OF NEW HAVEN FOR CONNECTICUT ENERGY ASSISTANCE PROGRAM 
(CEAP) PROGRAM YEAR 2026-2027 MILLER SENIOR CENTER 
 
3. ORDER APPROVING A MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING AND 
AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR TO SIGN THE AGREEMENT GENERATION 
POWER CT 
 
4. ORDER APPROVING A MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE 
TOWN OF HAMDEN AND BRIAN DOLAN 
  
Motion: Gallagher 
Second Foley 
Vote: All in favor, 0 opposed, 0 abstentions.  The motion to add the items passed 
unanimously. 
 
Majority Leader Gallagher made a motion to bundle items 1-4.   
Second: Parks   
Vote: All in favor, 0 opposed, 0 abstentions.  Motion to bundle passed 
unanimously. 
 
Pro Tem Cardwell then called for the vote to pass the items.   
Vote: All in favor, 0 opposed, 0 abstentions.  Items passed unanimously. 
  
      
9. NEW BUSINESS 
There was no new business for this evening’s meeting. 
  
10. UNFINISHED BUSINESS 
There was no unfinished business for this evening’s meeting.  
11. ADJOURNMENT 
Pro Tem Cardwell made a motion to adjourn the meeting at 10:21pm.
